[quote=the_crystalline_empire;61179868][b]Chapter 2: The summons[/b]

[spoiler]Indeed, by some unknown magic, Ivan casually forgot about the conversation that had taken place the night prior, as he arose from his bed and tiptoed around the room for fear of waking his roommate up.

You are awake, said a voice, startling him as he turned to face Leyoroy, who was indeed awake.

D-did I wake you? Asked Ivan in an apologetic tone.

Nah, replied Leyoroy, I was already awake.

Ivan breathed a sigh of relief as he turned once again to the sink and mirror that sat in the room.

I was thinking of our conversation last night, stated Leyoroy, mdoing some research, he continued, It seems that there is an active chapter of the NCAE here, he stated as if this was some light comment.

Ivan sighed as the memory of the last night walked into his head once more, Really? He stated, feigning interest between the bubbles of toothpaste.

Yeah, the club is called UWU, replied Leyoroy.

Isnt it actually OwO? Stated Ivan, finally doing away with the toothpaste.

Oh heavens no, replied Leyoroy, seeming slightly aghast at the mention of the word OwO, No, UWU is meant to be cute and funny, OwO is flirtatious in some manner, though of this I know not much about, he continued.

Huh, I did not know that, replied Ivan dryly, Anyways, you were saying about UWU?

Yes UWU, which stands for Understanding Wonderous Undertakings, replied Leyoroy.

And why does this matter? Asked Ivan, brushing his hair.

Because I emailed the president of the club last night after our conversation, and he is curious about you, stated Leyoroy

I am sorry, me? Replied Ivan, slightly confused, Why? How does he even know about me?!

Leyoroy laughed as he hopped off the bed, I told him about your sighting last night. 

So? Replied Ivan. Its a bit weird, he continued, moving to untie the bag that they had hung up to collect the blue ceiling drippings.

Anyways, they are meeting tonight, I think we should go, replied Leyoroy, ignoring Ivans seeming discomfort.

I have homework, replied Ivan bluntly, which was partially true, but it wasnt the type that wouldve taken all afternoon.

No, you dont, replied Leyoroy bluntly, seeing through his lie, So you will go? He stated.

Ivan sighed and replied, Only if you suffer with me also.

Leyoroy gave a big grin, Who says I will suffer? He laughed.

You are weird, beyond weird, replied Ivan, moving towards the door, I dont know how I stand you, he stated before opening it and leaving for the hallway, giving a hard stare at a disheveled figure who had just run down the hallway shouting something about weird figures in his mind.

 Ivan was not sure what to think about the events of the past two days, and the second day had yet to begin.[/spoiler][/quote]

[b]Chapter 3: The Rabbithole[/b]

[spoiler]The day dragged on for Ivan, whose mind caused it to be hard for him to focus on his classes, dull as they already were. His eyes moved across the crowds as he made his way across campus, inspecting his classes and his professors. He was not paranoid, but watchful, primarily because he had no desire to make contact with this group. Indeed, he was miffed at his roommate, going behind his back, contacting this group, and forcing him to go, yet Ivan was also curious, not in a scientific way but in the way that one might perhaps research a terrible incident. 

As evening came across the college, Ivan had determined to meet with his roommate at the dining hall before the first meeting of UWU, hoping to draw from him some sort of further information, or even a haha I was just kidding sort of matter. 

It was in this mindset that Ivan made haste across the campus beneath the wilding trees that hung low over the paths, their limbs and leaves scraping the ground with the breath of the wild wind. 

He wasnt paying attention and thus did not see the figures in the shadows of the buildings that surrounded the quad, watching his moves; these remained invisible even to the passersby who made way to their dorms and places of habitation. 

As he made his way through the grand archway that led off the quad, stepping up the steps into the plaza of the Doyland Richard plaza (for the man had donated some money towards the library, for a member of the board of curators was a friend of the man), Ivan suddenly felt a prickle on the back of his neck, stopping he heard a muffled sort of breathing as if it was coming from a mask. He picked up his pace, speed walking across the plaza towards the student center. 

He was running by the time he left the plaza and crossed the park that separated the student center from the rest of campus, his heart pounding in his chest, his breathing rapid, fear jolted into his heart and mind as he suddenly tripped and fell headlong across the grass, striking his face upon the ground. [/spoiler]

[spoiler=[b]Leipzig[/b]]
Responses to post: 

The use of home-on-jam missiles against the EA-18G Growlers would be largely ineffective. The use of DRFM jammers onboard the planes would allow the Growlers to change frequency, power, shift the direction of emissions and create false jamming sources to throw off the home-on-jam missiles which rely on a strong and stable jamming source. These allow the Growlers to create false targets, break lock and misdirect the HOJ missiles. In the exceptionally rare instances where the HOJs maintain a reliable lock on the Growlers, the planes simply turn off jamming and hand it over to a different platform such as a Compass Call. The SAMs attacking the Growlers quickly become targets of the SEAD assault. Their radar emissions burn bright as they track the Growlers, allowing the GJ-11 CCAs to perform reactive SEAD and launch REG-3000 anti-radiation missiles toward the SAMs. 

By switching to field telephones over traditional networks the Dutch had conceded a major advantage of modern warfare. The HDF would now be able to coordinate faster and exchange information more efficiently but the use of physical wires by the Dutch gave points of vulnerability as well. Wire laid down for communication would be identified by the RQ-170 UAV with the HAF following up with FAMM cruise missile strikes and loitering munition strikes to break enemy communications. The Dutch use of copper wires allowed the HDF to more easily snap them under pressure but also allowed the HDF to physically tap them using induction clamps to monitor calls. The creation of false command centers are largely ineffective. SIGINT of electronic emissions is one of the many tools of the Republiks military intelligence. Constant surveillance through RQ-170s and electro-optical satellites allowed the HDF to discern between real and false command centers to inform future strikes.

The Dutch strategy of air war would be quickly exploited by the HAF. Aircraft flying at low altitudes are limited due to radar being limited to the curvature of the earth. Republik CCAs flying at much higher altitudes are able to pick up the older jets much faster than the F-14ANs are able to see them or the Republiks jets behind the CCAs. With a time and stealth advantage the fifth generation jets of the HAF and the CCAs quickly pursue the threat. At before-visual range the Republik air force fires off BVRAAMs with a range of over 180 kilometres. Growlers in the strike packages contribute to the assault by spoofing jet radars and creating false targets to confuse the Dutch. SM-2s from the Navy's cruisers move as well to intercept the jets. Flying at high supersonic speeds (mach 3.5) and capable of high-G maneuvers the missiles quickly close with the F-14ANs. 

Continuation:

With the heavy weakening of the air defenses of the Dutch State and a persistent SEAD presence in Dutch airspace the fifth generation aircraft of the HAF moved closer to deliver greater blows to the Dutch. JA-35 jets using their internal bays deliver extended range JDAMs across the Dutch State to destroy the enemy's ability to wage war. 2,000 lb variants are used on rail yards, vital roads, bridges, tunnels and command centers to break the movement of thousands of troops across the country. CCAs are used to target fuel supplies for Dutch vehicles, strike Dutch armor using StormBreaker small diameter bombs and drop cluster munitions across the country to hit groups of enemy troops. For areas with a greater presence of air defenses the Donau-Klasse nuclear submarines continue to hit sites across the country with Tomahawk cruise missiles. 

Now that the majority of the navy has been forced to port by the Hochdeutsche Navies blockade the HDF pursued a policy of rapidly scrapping the remnants of the surface fleet. B-25EX stealth bombers would continue to drop 500-lb QUICKSINK JDAMs allowing them to strike 80 separate surface ships at the same time. Exploding at the hull the JDAMs are specially designed to breach the hulls of the ships and sink them. At port this becomes easier than ever. Naval strike missiles from expeditionary bases in Imerria join the salvo, using their sea skimming capabilities to avoid detection and strike the ships. The basis of the navy would be hit as well. Dry docks across the country would be targeted with FAMM cruise missiles and JDAMs to prevent the enemy from repairing damaged ships and submarines. Naval bases used for replenishment would also be targeted by the Air Forces cruise missile strikes. Towed sonar arrays aboard the Constellation frigates give the Navy a large advantage in anti-submarine warfare. The long trailing arrays are extremely sensitive to low frequency noises emitted from submarines. Sonobuoys dropped from P-8 Poseidons add another layer of detection as well as fixed seabed arrays installed by the UUVs. Long-range missiles such as the Republiks SMART fly at supersonic speeds towards the submarine's location and drop off a torpedo into the area to strike the submarine. On top of this the Republik utilizes swarms of UUVs to fire MK58 CRAW torpedoes towards the submarines. 

With heavy bombardment of Dutch forces and large scale assaults on the Dutch navy and air force the Republiks Marineinfantrie readied for a landing in the country. GJ-11s using JDAMs would strike Dutch naval artillery and coastal defences alongside Tomahawk cruise missiles. Dutch troops in the area would be hit with near constant bombardments from the cruisers with continuous Tomahawk strikes against entrenched positions, command centers and arms depots. Cluster munitions, each dumping hundreds of smaller bombs into the designated areas, are used to strike troops and vehicles. Again, the CCAs pour StormBreaker SDBs to hit Dutch armor while Harpy loitering munitions strike SAMs. UUVs work to dismantle mines through using neutralizer munitions to trigger the mines and cause them to prematurely detonate or be rendered ineffective. Then the assault would begin. The Marineinfantrie would be moved quickly to the beachhead via LCAC along with heavy armor. Additionally, ACVs would deploy from landing docks and move waves of Marineinfantrie to the shores while providing suppressive fire. Upon arriving at the beach, attack helicopters armed with hellfires and other munitions as well as JA-35s would provide constant close air support. Light MRZR vehicles and high speed Cottonmouth armored vehicles would allow the Marineinfantrie to quickly push inland and expand the beachhead. Within 24 hours the Republik would move 35,000 troops onto Dutch territory. 
[/spoiler]
